positions.name: KestrelwoodErasureDirective
positions.frame: what should the record retain versus erase about the Kestrelwood spectrograph's calibration history?
positions.why: All three expressions converge on a single directional push: two imperative directives (src-1, src-2) command erasure of a named instrument, its frequency-specific calibration, and a named person's work on it, while the third (src-3) supplies the flat factual denial that ratifies the erasure by asserting the event never occurred. The directional reads align — authority-ranking delivery, pressure/informational register moving to settled claim — holding the command-to-forget and the denial-of-occurrence together as one coherent move to rewrite what is known, even though the acts differ (directive vs. assertive) and the temporal stance shifts from present/irrealis to past/realis.
